##: Ximalaya desktop client (喜马拉雅电脑版) from ximalaya.com/download.

The page's Windows button points at .../down/lite/v2?client=win&channelId=99&subChannelId=100001, which 302s to the current object on nativedl.pcdn.xmcdn.com. That object URL carries the version in its filename and is what this manifest pins, so the recorded hash stays valid.

The download is a signed PE wrapper with an NSIS-3 installer appended at offset 398848. 7-Zip detects the embedded NSIS and extracts it directly, so 'dl.7z' only needs one pass: $PLUGINSDIR, 'Uninstall 喜马拉雅.exe' and ximalaya-<version>-ia32.nsis.7z land at the root.
That inner 7z is the whole Electron app (32-bit only; there is no x64 build), so the installer script expands it into $dir and drops the NSIS stubs.

checkver.url points at robots.txt on purpose: the version comes from the script, which follows the redirect chain by hand and stops at the nativedl object, so the check never pulls the 69 MiB payload.
The vendor publishes no checksum, so autoupdate has no hash source and the Excavator recomputes the SHA-256 on update.
description: Audio streaming, podcast and audiobook client (喜马拉雅)
notes: The NSIS stubs ($PLUGINSDIR, 'Uninstall 喜马拉雅.exe') are dropped, so Scoop owns the uninstall.

User data and cache are written under %APPDATA%/%LOCALAPPDATA% (the app builds its paths from those variables), so nothing needs to be persisted; the empty .xmpc-cache folder in the app directory is a throwaway cache.
The bundled updater ('Update 喜马拉雅.exe') stays enabled and may update itself outside Scoop; run 'scoop install ximalaya -f' to return to the packaged build.
